title_en: Xu Lei v. Zhonghui Real Estate Company — dispute over property ownership
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 41 of the Contract Law, if the lessee and lessor have not negotiated to exempt the lessor from the obligation to refund the deposit, and the lessor refuses to refund the deposit on the ground that the standard-form contract for termination of the house lease relationship provided by the lessor and signed by both parties contains a clause stating 'there is no further economic relationship between the parties,' and the lessee objects, the lessor cannot be exempted from the obligation to refund the deposit.

full_text_en:
Xu Lei v. Zhonghui Real Estate Company — Dispute over Property Ownership

Ruling Summary

Where the lessee and the lessor have not negotiated to exempt the lessor from the obligation to refund the security deposit, and the lessor refuses to refund the security deposit on the ground that a standard-form contract for the termination of the house lease relationship provided by the lessor and signed by both parties contains a clause stating that "there shall be no further economic relationship between the parties," and the lessee raises an objection, the lessor cannot be exempted from the obligation to refund the security deposit, in accordance with Article 41 of the Contract Law.

Plaintiff: Xu Lei, female, 40 years old, staff member of the Changsha Municipal People's Government Liaison Office in Beijing, residing in Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Defendant: Beijing Zhonghui Xinyuan Real Estate Brokerage Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Fengtai District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhang Bingxing, General Manager of the company.

Plaintiff Xu Lei filed a lawsuit with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing against Defendant Beijing Zhonghui Xinyuan Real Estate Brokerage Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhonghui Real Estate Company) due to a dispute over property ownership.

Plaintiff's Allegations: Because the plaintiff leased the defendant's house, the defendant collected a security deposit from the plaintiff. After the house lease contract between the parties was terminated, the defendant failed to refund the security deposit within one month as agreed. The plaintiff requested a judgment ordering the defendant to return the plaintiff's security deposit of RMB 1,600.

Defendant's Defense: The termination agreement signed by both parties explicitly stipulated that from the date of signing, there would be no further house lease relationship or economic relationship between the plaintiff and the defendant. The plaintiff's request for a refund of the security deposit after signing violated this agreement between the parties; therefore, the defendant disagreed with the plaintiff's claim.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing found the following facts upon trial:

Plaintiff Xu Lei, by signing a Beijing house lease contract, rented a one-bedroom apartment owned by Defendant Zhonghui Real Estate Company located at Zhichun Dongli, Haidian District, Beijing, with a lease term from October 8, 2003, to October 7, 2004, and a monthly rent of RMB 1,600. Article 3, Paragraph 3 of the lease contract stipulated: Party A (Xu Lei) shall pay Party B (Zhonghui Real Estate Company) a security deposit of RMB 1,600; within one month after the contract expires, Party B shall refund the security deposit to Party A after Party A settles the water, electricity, gas, cable television, and other fees incurred during the lease term. Appendix 5 stipulated: If Party A terminates the contract midway, Party A shall notify Party B one month in advance, and this shall not be deemed a breach of contract; otherwise, it shall be deemed a breach. Pursuant to the lease contract, Xu Lei paid the security deposit of RMB 1,600 to Zhonghui Real Estate Company. On December 5, 2003, Xu Lei applied to Zhonghui Real Estate Company for lease termination. On January 7, 2004, both parties inventoried the items in the leased premises and completed an item delivery checklist. On the same day, Xu Lei and Zhonghui Real Estate Company also signed a termination agreement, stipulating: From the date of signing this agreement, there shall be no further house lease relationship or economic relationship between the parties.

The above facts are confirmed by the statements of the parties, the Beijing house lease contract, the lease termination application, the item delivery checklist, the termination agreement, and other evidence.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing held:

Article 60, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law) provides: "The parties shall fully perform their obligations as agreed." The house lease contract and the termination agreement signed by Plaintiff Xu Lei and Defendant Zhonghui Real Estate Company represented the true intentions of both parties, did not violate legal provisions, were lawful and valid, and both parties should perform in accordance with the above agreements. In the termination agreement, both parties had explicitly agreed: From the date of signing, there shall be no further house lease relationship or economic relationship between the parties. After signing the agreement, Xu Lei's subsequent request for Zhonghui Real Estate Company to refund her security deposit lacked factual basis and legal grounds and was not supported.

Accordingly, the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing rendered a judgment on December 20, 2004: Rejecting Plaintiff Xu Lei's claim for Defendant Zhonghui Real Estate Company to refund the security deposit of RMB 1,600. The case acceptance fee of RMB 74 was borne by Plaintiff Xu Lei.

After the judgment was pronounced, Xu Lei was dissatisfied and appealed to the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court. The grounds for appeal were: I. Regarding the facts of the case. (1) The termination agreement signed by both parties did not contain any provisions regarding the security deposit; the security deposit receipt issued by the appellee was still in the appellant's possession; the appellee never indicated that the security deposit had been refunded or would not be refunded, and the appellant never indicated waiver of the right to the security deposit; (2) A security deposit legal relationship is not equivalent to an economic relationship; stating that there is no further economic relationship between the parties does not mean that the security deposit legal relationship does not exist; (3) The termination agreement was signed on January 7, 2004, but as late as January 14 of the same year, the appellee was still demanding that the appellant pay outstanding water and electricity charges from the lease term. After the appellant paid these charges, the appellee issued a receipt to the appellant. This indicates that the phrase "no further economic relationship" in the termination agreement did not include economic relationships for amounts payable or refundable that existed before the termination agreement was concluded. Therefore, when the appellant requested a refund of the security deposit, the appellee's refusal on this ground was untenable. The first instance court, lacking other corroborating evidence and relying solely on this phrase in the termination agreement, found that the security deposit legal relationship between the parties no longer existed, which constituted a finding of unclear facts. II. Regarding the application of law. (1) Article 66 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings" states: "Judicial personnel shall comprehensively examine and assess all evidence in a case based on the degree of relevance of each piece of evidence to the facts of the case and the connections between the pieces of evidence." In the lawsuit for the refund of the security deposit brought by the appellant, the appellant submitted the original security deposit receipt, while the appellee did not submit any evidence that the security deposit had been refunded or that the appellant had waived the right to the security deposit. Under these circumstances, the first instance court's finding that "no further economic relationship" encompassed the security deposit relationship, thereby dismissing the appellant's claim, constituted illegal evaluation of evidence. (2) The RMB 1,600 was a security deposit under the house lease contract, and its ownership necessarily always belonged to the appellant; the appellee only temporarily exercised possession of this sum during the existence of the lease relationship, and the ownership of the sum did not transfer. Article 98 of the Contract Law provides: "The termination of rights and obligations under a contract does not affect the validity of the contract's settlement and liquidation clauses." The house lease contract signed by both parties contained an agreement to refund the security deposit within one month after the contract terminated; these were the settlement and liquidation clauses of the contract, and the termination of the contract should not affect the validity of these clauses. The first instance court's judgment dismissing the appellant's claim under Article 60 of the Contract Law constituted an error in the application of law and should be corrected. Accordingly, the appellant requested that the second instance court set aside the first instance judgment, amend the judgment to support the appellant's claim, and order the appellee to bear the litigation costs of both the first and second instances.

Appellee Zhonghui Real Estate Company argued in response that it agreed with the first instance judgment.

The Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, upon trial, confirmed the facts found by the first instance court and further found: On January 7, 2004, the item delivery checklist completed by both parties after inventorying the items in the leased premises recorded the following: water meter start reading 1479, end reading 1483; gas meter start reading 1440, end reading 1456; except for two loose wall tiles in the bathroom, there were no other damages to items in the premises. On January 14 of the same year, Appellant Xu Lei paid outstanding water and gas charges totaling RMB 28 to Appellee Zhonghui Real Estate Company, as confirmed by a receipt issued by Zhonghui Real Estate Company. The relevant Beijing house lease contract, termination agreement, lease termination application, item delivery checklist, and other documents involved in this case were all pre-printed by Zhonghui Real Estate Company and filled in at the time of use.

The focus of the dispute in this case was: How should the clause in the termination agreement stating "there shall be no further house lease relationship or economic relationship between the parties" be interpreted? Did Zhonghui Real Estate Company have the obligation to refund the security deposit?

The Beijing First Intermediate People's Court held:

The security deposit in a house lease contract is property mortgaged by the lessee to the lessor to ensure the lessee's performance of obligations under the lease contract. Once the lessee has performed its obligations under the lease contract, the lessor shall refund the security deposit to the lessee. A comprehensive examination and assessment of all evidence in this case leads to the conclusion that, after the house lease contract terminated, Appellant Xu Lei neither damaged the leased premises or items therein, nor had any outstanding fees to pay, nor indicated any waiver of her right to the security deposit. Yet, Zhonghui Real Estate Company did not refund the RMB 1,600 mortgaged by Xu Lei to the company. The sole reason for the company's refusal to refund the security deposit was the clause in the termination agreement stating "there shall be no further house lease relationship or economic relationship between the parties."

Under ordinary interpretation, a security deposit legal relationship constitutes an economic relationship; since the parties have no further economic relationship, this naturally includes no further security deposit legal relationship. However, the payment and collection of water and gas charges also constitute an economic relationship. After signing the agreement stating "no further economic relationship," the parties still made and accepted payments for these two charges, indicating that their understanding of "no further economic relationship" was inconsistent with common sense. Appellant Xu Lei believed that "no further economic relationship" did not include the security deposit legal relationship; Appellee Zhonghui Real Estate Company, while asserting that "no further economic relationship" included the security deposit legal relationship, nevertheless, through its conduct of collecting charges, excluded the payment and collection of water and gas charges from the category of economic relationships. The interpretations of this clause by both parties were diametrically opposed.

The Beijing house lease contract and the termination agreement involved in this case were both standard-form contracts provided by Appellee Zhonghui Real Estate Company to Appellant Xu Lei. Except for the disputed interpretation of the clause "there shall be no further house lease relationship or economic relationship between the parties" in the termination agreement, both parties had consistent interpretations of the other clauses, and the remaining clauses of the two contracts were lawful and valid. Article 3 of the Contract Law provides: "The parties to a contract have equal legal status, and one party may not impose its will on the other party." Article 41 provides: "If a dispute arises over the interpretation of a standard clause, the clause shall be interpreted in accordance with its ordinary meaning. If there are two or more interpretations of a standard clause, an interpretation unfavorable to the party that provided the standard clause shall prevail. If a standard clause is inconsistent with a non-standard clause, the non-standard clause shall prevail." At the time of signing the termination agreement, Zhonghui Real Estate Company was aware that the security deposit collected under the lease contract had not yet been refunded and that the receipt for the RMB 1,600 security deposit was still in Xu Lei's possession. As the provider of the standard-form contract, if Zhonghui Real Estate Company believed that the standard clause "there shall be no further house lease relationship or economic relationship between the parties" carried the meaning that the security deposit would not be refunded, it had the obligation to remind Xu Lei of this fact or to note in the agreement that, upon signing this clause, the security deposit would no longer be refunded and the security deposit receipt would be invalidated. Zhonghui Real Estate Company did not fulfill this obligation. Given that the termination agreement made no mention whatsoever of how the security deposit or the security deposit receipt should be handled, the wording of the standard clause "there shall be no further house lease relationship or economic relationship between the parties" does not directly lead to the inference that Xu Lei had the intention to voluntarily waive her right to the security deposit. Therefore, under the circumstances where the lease contract had terminated and the outstanding fees had been paid, Zhonghui Real Estate Company's refusal to refund the security deposit based solely on Xu Lei's signing of the termination agreement lacked legal basis and constituted an infringement of Xu Lei's property ownership.

In summary, Appellant Xu Lei's appeal grounds that Appellee Zhonghui Real Estate Company should refund her security deposit of RMB 1,600 were well-founded and should be adopted. The facts found by the first instance court were essentially clear, but the application of law was erroneous, and the result of the judgment was improper, which should be corrected in accordance with the law. Accordingly, the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a judgment on April 20, 2005:

1. Setting aside the civil judgment of the first instance;
2. Appellee Zhonghui Real Estate Company shall pay Appellant Xu Lei a security deposit of RMB 1,600 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect.
   The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances, each RMB 74, shall be borne by Appellee Zhonghui Real Estate Company.
   This judgment is final.
